messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — vendor sent an updated commitment draft 10m ago. Key change is a "surge protection" carveout that limits guaranteed GPU hours during peak season. Link: https://example.cloud/commitments (redacted)
kenji: Ugh. Do they define "peak season" or caps? that could wreck our canary/burst plans
maria: They added this section: ```Surge Protection: Provider may limit committed capacity up to 20% during provider-declared peak events for up to 14 consecutive days per quarter.```
kenji: That 20% + 14d is not acceptable. Our safety stock assumptions rely on at least 95% availability of committed units year-round
dave: Can we get a hard SLA for minimum throughput instead of a generic "may limit" clause? e.g., 95% of committed vGPU hours per month with credits
sophia: +1 for throughput SLA. Also ask for a notification window and automatic failover credits if they preempt dedicated capacity without 72h notice
maria: Logged those asks. Sales rep said they'd push but vendor legal flagged risk. Re the credit ask: they offered a sliding credit up to 10% of monthly fee, but only if outage > 48h
kenji: Sliding credit starting at 48h is too late. We need a graduated credit model that starts at 1h and scales. Otherwise our cost model for customer SLAs breaks
cloud-sales-bot: Note: previous EDP with vendor-xyz included a 99.5% committed-hour SLA and 5% credits for 4h outages. See internal doc: /policies/edp-archive
dave: Proposed counter: 1) Replace "may limit" with explicit preemption triggers (e.g., regional emergency / maintenance) 2) Minimum monthly committed-hour SLA = 99% 3) Graduated credits: 1-4h=2%, 4-24h=10%, >24h=25% 4) 72h advance notice for non-emergency capacity reduction
sophia: Also push for spot-to-dedicated conversion clause: if capacity constrained, provider must offer equivalent instance types in region or provide cross-region failover at no extra charge for 7 days
maria: I like that. Also asking for a capped monthly ramp-up tolerance — we need predictable on-ramps for Dedicated customers. Add "ramp guarantee": first 30 days of each quarter provider will provide additional up to 15% of committed capacity on request within 7 business days
kenji: We should prepare numbers: ask for 15% ramp and simulate billing impact. I can run a quick model today
dave: Also legal asked to tighten termination protections — if they materially change availability terms we get pro-rated termination + data egress credit
maria: Action items:
- @kenji run billing/availability model showing cost impact of 20% preemption vs proposed SLA (due EOD)
- @sophia draft language for spot-to-dedicated/cross-region failover
- @dave add termination/egress clause wording and credits for legal review
- I will push counter-proposal to vendor by EOD and ask for a weekly sync
sophia: noted. I'll pull recent incident history to support ask for lower preemption window
kenji: Model started — initial result: 20% preemption increases 99th pct latency risk and requires ~18% extra safety stock to maintain 95% availability. Will post numbers in thread soon
maria: Thanks. If vendor pushes back hard on legal language, plan B is: accept 10% capped surge for non-emergency, but demand 99% monthly SLA + immediate credits and cross-region failover. Prefer not to sign otherwise :thumbsup:
sophia: pls cc sales ops and account team on final
cloud-sales-bot: Reminder: schedule created: negotiation-sync w/ vendor at 2026-05-12T16:00Z. Meeting link will be posted.
maria: Perfect — I'll circulate the counter and sync invite. End.
